newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares lose 0.8 pct in profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares lose 0.8 pct in profit-taking.

text.p: Istanbul shares fell an average 0.77 percent in quiet profit-taking on Tuesday after resistance at the index's 78,500 level prompted sales following an early rally, brokers said.
They said the market grew cautious ahead of Wednesday's parliamentary debate on a censure motion against Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, following his controversial trip to Libya.

The IMKB-100 closed at 77,412.15, down 603.47 points from Monday when it leapt 2.4 percent on expectations that the Islamist-led government would not be affected by the motion. The index dived from a morning high of 79,157.
Trading volume shrank to 13.8 trillion lira from Monday's 16.7 trillion.
"Today's fluctuations were normal developments ahead of the censure motion," said Nazmi Sarikaya from Disbank securities.
"If the motion is rejected in parliament, an upward move towards 80,000 is possible because main players are long in shares," he added.
The market index dived 4.2 percent on Thursday and Friday after soaring 22.7 percent from September 13 to last Wednesday's sixth consecutive all-time high close of 79,511.82 in a strong uptrend.

Brokers who await support of the index at 76,000 and then at around 75,000, said the index could be stuck in a range at between 75,000 and 79,000 in the coming days with players switching to smaller stocks from those carrying high premiums.

Of the 225 shares traded, 110 declined, 60 advanced and 55 finished stable. The 85-share industrial index eased 0.38 percent to 83,214.63 and the 15-share financial index dropped 1.68 percent to 72,038.27.

Top actives were cement pipe and brick producer Dogusan, down 4,000 lira at 70,000, iron and steel firm Metas, up 1,300 lira at 7,000, utilities Kepez Elektrik, down 1,000 lira at 85,000 and its associate Cukurova Elektrik, down 2,000 lira at 71,000, largely state-owned flat steel giant Eregli, up 100 lira at 9,600.
